Java Swing GUI Guide

Learn what GUI components are, then build a Swing login page and welcome page step by step in NetBeans. Use this guide while you work on Task 1 (reusable components) and Task 3 (Java GUI) of the Excellent Restaurant Reservation System GA.

① What are GUI components?

Start here. Understand the idea first, then the code will make sense.

The idea

GUI = Graphical User Interface

A GUI is the part of a program you can see and click: windows, buttons, text boxes, pictures and menus. Instead of typing commands, the user points, clicks and types into boxes.

Each visible piece of a GUI (a button, a text box, a label) is called a GUI component. In Java, these components come from a library called Swing (javax.swing). Their names usually start with J: JFrame, JButton, JTextField...

How a GUI reacts

Events: “when the user does X, run code Y”

GUI programs are event-driven. The program waits. When the user clicks, types or moves the mouse, an event happens, and Java runs the method you wrote for it (the event handler).

☕ Event demo–☐✕
1. User clicksthe Show button
→
2. ActionEventJava creates an event
→
3. Handler runsbtnShowActionPerformed()
→
4. Resultmessage is shown
private void btnShowActionPerformed(java.awt.event.ActionEvent evt) {
    String name = txtName.getText();      // read the text box
    String course = txtCourse.getText();

    JOptionPane.showMessageDialog(this,
            "Name: " + name + "\nCourse: " + course,
            "Entered Details",
            JOptionPane.INFORMATION_MESSAGE);
}
✅

Foreground events come from the user (click, key press, scroll). Background events happen without the user (a timer finishing, a system interrupt). Your 60-second “Time Out!” in Task 3 is a background event from a Timer.

Quiz: name that component

GA helper · Task 1

From “components” to “reusable components”

A reusable component is a ready-made piece of software (a class, library, module or API) that someone already built and tested, so you can use it again instead of writing it from zero.

Every Swing component above is a reusable component: you did not write JButton, you just reuse it. Libraries from outside Java (for example a date-picker library) are reusable components too.

🎯

⚖️ Task 1.3: the 6 evaluation questions explained

Functionality

Does it do the job we need? Say what it does for the user.

Compatibility

Does it work with Java, Swing, NetBeans and our Java version?

Security

Any known weakness? e.g. does a password box hide the text? Is the library maintained?

Ease of integration

Can we add it easily? (drag from Palette = very easy; download a .jar = more steps)

Dependencies

Does it need other libraries/imports or files (e.g. a .wav file, a .jar) to work?

Reusability

Can we use it again in other forms/projects without big changes?

📝 Worked example (a different feature, so you can copy the method, not the answer)

Functionality: “Customer feedback form”. Component being evaluated: JTextArea.

CriterionExample answer for JTextArea
FunctionalityYes – lets the customer type a long comment on many lines.
CompatibilityYes – part of Java Swing (javax.swing), works in any Java desktop app and in the NetBeans designer.
SecurityNo known vulnerabilities; it is part of the standard JDK. The text must still be validated before saving.
Ease of integrationVery easy – drag it from the Palette; read the text with getText().
DependenciesOnly the JDK. Best placed inside a JScrollPane so long text can scroll.
ReusabilityHigh – the same component can be reused in any form that needs multi-line input.
📚

Write the answers in your own words and add the References row (e.g. Oracle Java documentation links in Section 3). Grade A needs sources correctly referenced.

Create a Java project

  1. Open NetBeans → File → New Project.
  2. Choose Java with Ant → Java Application → Next.
  3. Give the project a name related to the restaurant.
  4. Untick “Create Main Class” – each JFrame Form already has its own main → Finish.
📁

Remember where the project folder is saved. Later you will put your logo and sound files inside it.

Add the two JFrame Forms

  1. In the Projects panel, right-click your package (or Source Packages).
  2. New → JFrame Form. If you don't see it: New → Other → Swing GUI Forms → JFrame Form.
  3. Name the first one for the login window → Finish.
  4. Do it again for the welcome window.
💡

Now your project has two classes. Each one is its own window, with its own Design view and its own Source code.

Know the NetBeans screen

Source / Design tabs

Design = drag and drop (you will spend most of your time here). Source = the Java code.

Palette

The box of components (Label, Button, Text Field...). Drag from here onto the form.

Properties

Change the selected component: text, font, colours, icon...

Navigator

A list of every component in the form, with its variable name.

⚠️

Everything you drag and drop is written for you by NetBeans inside the grey (locked) code. Don't try to edit it. You will only type code inside event methods and in a few places outside the grey blocks.

All of this is done with the mouse – no typing code:

🧭 Check names

Look in the Navigator – every component should have a meaningful name.

A good habit: start each name with a short prefix that tells the type, then what it is for.

🏷️ JLabel → lbl…
✍️ JTextField → txt…
🔒 JPasswordField → txt… / pwd…
🔘 JButton → btn…
🟦 JPanel → pnl…
🖼️ Logo label → lbl…Logo
⚠️

Rename before you add events. NetBeans uses the variable name to name the event method (e.g. a button called btnLogin gets btnLoginActionPerformed).

Add the restaurant logo

  1. Make a folder images inside your project's src folder and copy the logo file into it.
  2. Select the logo Label → delete its text.
  3. Properties → icon → click ...
  4. Choose Image Within Project → select your logo → OK.
📏

A JLabel shows the picture at its real size, so resize the image file first (around 200 px wide). Standard: logo top-left or centered in the header, not covering the form fields.

Plan your class: variables and methods

Before adding events, plan what your login class needs. The GA asks for these parts:

LoginPage (your class name)
Instance variables in the class, outside methods
• the correct username (a String, with a starting value)
• the correct password (a String, with a starting value)
Methods each does one job
• a method to verify the username and password → answers true / false
• a method to play the sound
Local variables inside a method
• the parameters of your methods (e.g. the typed username and password)

Where?

In Source, just under the line public class … extends javax.swing.JFrame { – outside the grey code.

Methods go…

inside the class, but not inside another method. Below the constructor is a good place.

Initialize

Give every variable a starting value. Task 3.2-j asks for a screenshot of this.

📖

Not sure how to write a method that takes parameters and returns a boolean? Look back at your Unit 07 notes on methods and return types.

Add a click event (from the Design view)

  1. In Design, double-click the button.
    or right-click → Events → Action → actionPerformed
  2. NetBeans jumps to Source and creates an empty event method for that button.
  3. Your cursor is already between the { }. Your code goes there.
🔁

Do this for every button: Log In, Clear, the 4 service buttons and Back. The GA says all button clicks must be handled by event handlers.

🧰 Tools you will need

getText() reads a text field
getPassword() reads a password field (gives a char array – turn it into a String)
isEmpty() / trim() check for empty text
equals() compares two Strings
JOptionPane.showMessageDialog() shows a message (see Section 1 for the types)
setText("") empties a box – for the Clear button

Compare Strings with equals(), never with ==. Using == is a classic logic error – a good example for Task 4!

Move between the two windows

Each window is a separate class, so moving between them means: create the other window, show it, close this one.

3️⃣ Close this onedispose()

In the Log In event

After a successful login → open the welcome window, close the login window.

In the Back event

On the welcome window → open the login window again, close the welcome window.

💡

Inside a JFrame's own code, the word this means “this window”.

The 4 service buttons

In the welcome window, each service button's event shows a message box, like the examples below. Click them to preview:

Play a sound on successful login

  1. Put a .wav file in your project, e.g. in a sounds folder (MP3 will not work).
  2. Add the sound imports at the top of the Source (javax.sound.sampled and java.io.File).
  3. Write your play sound method (from your class plan) using a Clip from AudioSystem.
  4. Call that method in the success part of the Log In event.
🧠

How a Clip works: get a clip → open it with the audio file → start it. Because opening a file can fail, the code must sit inside try { } catch { }.

🔇

No sound? Check the file really is .wav, the path matches the folder name exactly, and read the Output window for an error message.

Show “Time Out!” after 60 seconds idle

⏱️ The component

javax.swing.Timer – runs an action after a delay.

⏳ The delay

Given in milliseconds: 1 second = 1000 ms, so 60 seconds = ?

📍 Where

In the JFrame constructor, after the line initComponents();

💬 The action

Show a message box: “Time Out!”

📖

Your GA Lab Activity slides 13–16 show how to create, start and use a Timer, including the short form e -> for an action listener.

💡

Think about it: a timer repeats by default – how can you make it fire only once? And “idle” means the user did nothing – what should happen to the timer when the user clicks a button? (Look up setRepeats and restart in the Oracle Timer page, Section 3.)

⏳ See the behaviour (10-second demo)

⚠️

Java has more than one class called Timer. Make sure you import the Swing one.

Comments: explain each block of your code

Comments are notes for humans – Java ignores them. The GA wants comments on different blocks (3 or more for grade B).

//

Single-line comment – one short note.

/* … */

Multi-line comment – explains a whole block.

/** … */

Javadoc – describes what a method does.

✅ Good comment

Says why / what: “Check that the username box is not empty”

❌ Weak comment

Just repeats the code: “if statement”

🗂️

Good places for comments: above your instance variables, above each method, inside each event method, above the timer.

Run, test and collect your evidence

  1. Right-click the login JFrame file → Run File (Shift+F6).
  2. Test with empty fields, a wrong password and the correct password.
  3. Click each service button and the Back button on the welcome window.
  4. Leave it for 60 seconds without touching it → “Time Out!” should appear.
  5. Run → Clean and Build Project (Shift+F11) → find the .class files in build/classes (Task 4-a).
⚙️

To make the login window open first when you press the big green Run button: right-click project → Properties → Run → Main Class → choose your login JFrame.
